checks.title: FC ESC socket vs ESC socket vs the lead
checks.evidence: ESC socket positions 1-8: Curr, NC, M4, M3, M2, M1, VBAT, GND (maker drawing). FC socket positions 1-8: Curr, RX7, M4, M3, M2, M1, VBAT, GND (ArduPilot port diagram, silk "C R 4 3 2 1 V G"). Maker wiring diagram draws a straight lead. On the robot both boards face rear with the sockets on the same (bottom) edge and in the same left-right order, so a straight lead (position n to n) is correct.
checks.open: Whether the stack box contains the 8-pin lead is not stated (listing: "1 x MicoAir 743 V2 Stack"); the SH kit in the cart makes one either way.

checks.title: ArduPilot Quad-X numbering, spin, ESC pad sets
checks.evidence: AP_MotorsMatrix QUAD X: motor 1 at +45 deg (front right) CCW, motor 2 at -135 (rear left) CCW, motor 3 at -45 (front left) CW, motor 4 at +135 (rear right) CW. ESC stood behind the right arm with tabs up puts pad sets 1 and 2 on the outboard (right) edge and 3 and 4 on the inboard edge, so outputs are remapped: SERVO1_FUNCTION 33 (pad 1 -> FR, motor 1), SERVO2_FUNCTION 36 (pad 2 -> RR, motor 4), SERVO3_FUNCTION 35 (pad 3 -> FL, motor 3), SERVO4_FUNCTION 34 (pad 4 -> RL, motor 2). CW units go front-left and rear-right, CCW units front-right and rear-left (spin seen from above = from the inlet, since the inlets face up). Direction: an EDF rotor is handed, so each unit must turn its own way to blow down; set it by swapping two leads at the bullets (ArduPilot wiki) or the AM32 "Reversed" box (MicoAir AM32 page).
checks.open: Which way QX means by "CW" (from the inlet or the exhaust) is not published: confirm at the first motor test (air must leave downward; the unit's rotation seen from above must match the map). If both CW units turn out CCW seen from above, swap the fans left-right between nacelles (no part changes). Pad 1 = connector M1 is the silkscreen convention; Mission Planner motor test confirms output-to-pad before any fan is mounted.

checks.title: MTF-01 pinout, voltage, UART, ArduPilot parameters
checks.evidence: MTF-01 SH1.0-4P: GND, 5V, Rx, Tx; supply 5 V, about 100 mA; LVTTL 3.3 V UART 115200. FC UART4 socket GND, 5V, TX4, RX4 (5 V from the FC 5 V/3 A BEC). MicoAir draws exactly this pairing for the MicoAir743 (straight lead). ArduPilot: SERIAL4_PROTOCOL 1, SERIAL4_BAUD 115, SERIAL4_OPTIONS 1024, FLOW_TYPE 5, RNGFND1_TYPE 10, RNGFND1_MIN_CM 1, RNGFND1_MAX_CM 800, RNGFND1_ORIENT 25 (maker guide; MIN_CM/MAX_CM still exist in Copter 4.6.3).
checks.open: FLOW_ORIENT_YAW depends on how CAD turns the module on the shelf (ArduPilot default: heading points from the lenses toward the chip side, maker image).

checks.title: A7Z to FC MAVLink link
checks.evidence: Free A7Z pins: 14 (GND), 16 (PJ24, UART4-TX), 18 (PJ25, UART4-RX); not in the as-built 19-wire map (used: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 9 11 12 17 25 29 31 34 35 38 39 40). UART2 (pins 7/11) carries the servo bus and is not touched; UART3 is on the IMU pins 3/5; UART0 (8/10) is the debug console. Radxa's stock overlay sun60iw2p1-uart4 ("Enable UART4", compatible radxa,cubie-a7z, "pin 16 and pin 18") gives /dev/ttyAS4. Levels: PJ bank VCC-PJ = VCC33-LCD 3.3 V (schematic V1.11); STM32H743 UART at 3.3 V; no level shifter needed. FC: SERIAL1 (UART1), default MAVLink2.
checks.open: A spare UART has never been enabled on this A7Z: CURRENT-STATE lists only the TWI7, TWI0, I2S0 overlays and UART2; no session enabled uart4 (transcript search "ttyAS4": documentation mentions only). The A7Z was offline on 2026-11-10 (ssh timeout), so /dev/ttyAS* was not read. Physical access to pins 14/16/18 in the saddle (edge row) not seen on the robot. 921600 baud on the A7Z UART is untested (115200 fallback).

checks.title: Two packs in parallel into the ESC tabs; currents vs ratings
checks.evidence: Mass used: v6 CAD 1888 g all-up with 80 g fans (2020 g with 113 g fans); hover thrust 472-505 g per fan. Hover current per fan 13.0-26.5 A (three methods: {'vendor': [13.0, 14.4], 'bench': [23.9, 26.5], 'momentum': [22.9, 25.3]}), total 52-106 A. Peak per fan 45 A (listing max continuous), 180 A total uncapped. Right pack share 54% (shorter pigtail). Per pack: hover 28.2-57.4 A, peak 97.6 A uncapped, 59.6 A with MOT_BAT_CURR_MAX 110. Ratings: ESC 55 A per channel vs fan 45 A max: pass. Pack 130C x 1.3 Ah = 169 A claimed: pass. XT60 (Amass) rated 30 A, max 60 A: hover may exceed the 30 A rating on the worst case; peaks stay at or under 60 A only with the MOT_BAT_CURR_MAX cap. 12 AWG chassis 41 A: hover at most at that rating, flights 1-1.5 min. 16 AWG chassis 22 A vs per-fan hover rms (0.82 x DC in six-step) and 45 A bursts: see motor_leads. Harness: one male XT60 pigtail per pack, both soldered to the same ESC tab pair; no Y-splice.
checks.open: The hover current spans 2x between methods (13 vs 26 A per fan) and decides the outcome. Low case (about 52 A total): each XT60 carries about 28 A, inside its 30 A rating, and the 110 A cap leaves 2x control headroom. High case (about 106 A total): each XT60 carries about 57 A continuous, at its 60 A maximum, and the 110 A cap leaves almost no headroom, so the cap would have to rise and the XT60s would run above rating; the fix then is soldering the pack leads straight to the pigtails or XT90 connectors (no change to what is ordered: the packs and wire stay the same). Decided by the first tethered hover: read BATT current (after BATT_AMP_PERVLT 78.43) and feel the XT60 bodies after 60 s. A flight-envelope limit, not a wiring blocker.

checks.title: Capacitor place, polarity, lead length
checks.evidence: Across the ESC battery tabs, as the maker diagram shows; 35 V on a 16.8 V pack. CAD places it lying on the right arm top flange, lead end about 30 mm from the + tab: each leg reaches the tab with a short 16 AWG extension if the leg is shorter, soldered on the tab together with the two pigtails. Long leg / side without the stripe to +. Left battery loop is long (about 0.3 m with the pack lead); forum practice adds 220-440 uF per 10 cm beyond 40 cm: 1000 uF low-ESR at the tabs covers it, and the right pack (short lead) sits in parallel.
checks.open: Rubycon leg length not published; if the legs reach the tabs directly, no extension and two fewer joints. Moving the capacitor so its legs touch the tabs is a CAD option.

checks.title: Ground and supply separation between duck and flight pack
checks.evidence: Joined: exactly one conductor, FC UART1 position 1 (GND) to A7Z pin 14 (GND), plus the two UART signal lines. Open: FC UART1 position 2 (5V); A7Z 5 V pins 2/4 untouched; no other conductor between the systems (printed frame, no metal path). No loop in flight: the only return path between the two negatives is that one 28 AWG wire, and no load current has a reason to flow in it. Back-feed: no 5 V or VBAT crosses. The one weak case: with the A7Z off and the FC powered, FC TX1 idles at 3.3 V into PJ25 of an unpowered SoC (through its protection diode, a few mA). Rule: duck on before the flight packs, flight packs off first (or unplug the 3-pin lead).
checks.open: If the FC USB and an A7Z USB cable go to the same Mac at the same time, the Mac ground joins them a second time: harmless at bench currents, do not hover like that.

checks.title: Motor lead length and extensions
checks.evidence: Fan leads about 70 mm (not published; photo estimate). Routed lengths from the CAD geometry (x1.15): FR 156 mm -> extension 100 mm, RR 46 mm -> extension 40 mm, FL 330 mm -> extension 280 mm, RL 220 mm -> extension 160 mm (CAD agent claimed FL 250, RL 200, FR 80, RR 50). Every fan needs an extension: 16 AWG silicone, female bullet at the fan end, soldered to the ESC pad. Factory leads look about 1.7 mm OD (about 18 AWG, inference), so 16 AWG does not bottleneck them. 16 AWG over 0.29 m at 45 A: 13.2 mOhm/m, two phases conduct, drop about 0.34 V (2.3 %); rms per phase about 37 A, above the 22 A chassis figure, so full throttle is a burst of seconds; hover rms 10-20 A is within it. Long motor leads with short battery leads is the ESC-friendly split; here the left side has both, unavoidable with one ESC on the right.
checks.open: Bullet size: the listing does not say; photo scale points to 2.0 mm, not the 3.5 mm the CAD agent assumed. Measure on arrival; MISSING.md buys both sizes so either fits.

checks.title: HTRC B6 V2 charges the 4S packs
checks.evidence: Listing: "LiPo: 1-6 cells", 80 W 6 A; images show 2S to 6S JST-XH balance ports (4S port labelled), 4 mm banana outputs and a "Connector Splitter" lead with an XT60 plug; box: charger, crocodile clip lead, connector splitter, 15 V 6 A adapter, AC cable. 4S at 1C (1.3 A) is 22 W, far under 80 W. Charge the packs one at a time, never through the flight harness.
checks.open: Gender of the splitter XT60 not visible (charge leads are normally male, matching the female pack plug).

checks.title: Arm and stop without an RC receiver
checks.evidence: No extra hardware. Parameters (Copter 4.6.3 sources): FS_THR_ENABLE 0 (no RC throttle failsafe); ARMING_CHECK with bit 6 "RC Channels" cleared (1047998 = all individual checks except RC); arm, mode changes and take-off from the A7Z over MAVLink (MAV_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM, GUIDED, MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF); stop = disarm, force with param2 21196; FS_GCS_ENABLE 5 (Land), FS_GCS_TIMEOUT 2 (minimum); the A7Z is the GCS (heartbeats at sysid 255 = SYSID_MYGCS default) and must land on its own if the web page stops (the FC only sees the A7Z). GCS failsafe only arms after a GCS has been seen, which arming from the A7Z guarantees. The board has no safety switch.
checks.open: Bench test before the first hover: kill the web page -> A7Z lands; kill the A7Z link -> FC lands after 2 s.

checks.title: Battery current scale (found while checking)
checks.evidence: ArduPilot default BATT_AMP_PERVLT 40.2 belongs to another ESC; this ESC outputs 12.75 mV/A, so the value is 1000 / 12.75 = 78.43 A/V. Until set, current, mAh and MOT_BAT_CURR_MAX read about half the truth.
checks.open: Set BATT_AMP_PERVLT 78.43 at setup; check against a clamp meter or the charger's mAh refill.

checks.title: AM32 motor poles and KV (found while checking)
checks.evidence: QF2611 is 9N6P (6 magnet poles); AM32 default is 14 poles, KV 2220 (MicoAir). Set Motor poles 6 and KV 4000 in AM32 on all four ESCs, and SERVO_BLH_POLES 6 in ArduPilot for bidirectional DShot RPM.
checks.open: Set through ArduPilot BLHeli passthrough (SERVO_BLH_AUTO 1) and the AM32 configurator.
